summary: Map.has checks whether a key exists independently of the value stored there.
documentation: Map.has checks whether a key exists independently of the value stored there. This distinguishes an absent setting from a present key whose value is null, false or zero. Map keys use SameValueZero equality and object keys compare by identity.
inputs: An object with pairs (string-key/value pairs) and queries (array of string keys).
returns: A Boolean for each queried key.
caution: Testing get(key) for truthiness confuses presence with a falsey value. This exercise uses strings as keys and plain JSON values.
scenarios: Distinguish an explicitly disabled feature from an unconfigured option.
Check whether a local cache has an entry even when the cached result is null.
Identify known imported keys before choosing a fallback value.
title: Check key presence
problem: Build a Map from input.pairs. For each string in input.queries, return whether that key exists, regardless of its stored value. Preserve query order.
goal: Use Map.has() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
